The Commission examined privity of contract in this case in a completely different context. The Petitioner has no concern with the recovery to be made by the Respondent from IPCL/SPTPL or action taken against IPCL/SPTPL. None of the judgments relied upon by the Respondent exonerates the Party to the contract for the default of the principal agreement. Thus, the reliance of the Respondent on EBA-2 to justify its defaults is untenable and unjustified.

12. The matter was heard along with Petition No. 94/MP/2023, 277/MP/2022, 282/MP/2022 & 265/MP/2022. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Respondent, SPTPL, submitted that certain settlement discussions are underway between the Respondent and HPPC and that the Respondent, on 4.10.2023, has submitted its revised proposal to HPPC, which has yet to respond thereto. In response, the learned counsel for HPPC submitted that there is no concrete proposal from the Respondent that is acceptable to HPPC and by not filing the reply in these matters, the Respondent is merely delaying the proceedings.

13. After hearing the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, the Commission expressed strong displeasure at the failure of Respondents, SPTPL and IPCL, to abide by the directions issued by the Commission vide the Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 21.7.2023. The Commission, however, deemed it appropriate to afford one last opportunity to all the parties to complete the pleadings in these matters and directed Respondents therein to file their comprehensive replies, with a copy to the other side, who may file their rejoinder.

17. After hearing the learned counsels for the parties, the Commission directed the parties to ensure the completion of the pleadings in these cases and file their respective reply and/or rejoinder, if any, with a copy to the other side.

18. The matters were again heard on 6.2.2025. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner/Respondent, KEIPL, requested an adjournment in the matters due to the non-availability of KEIPL’s Managing Director on serious medical grounds. The said request was not opposed by the learned counsel for the other side, and accordingly, these matters were adjourned. The matter was finally heard on 7.5.2025. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner, HPPC, and the Respondent, APPCPL, made detailed submissions and concluded their respective arguments. Considering their request, the Commission permitted the parties to file their note of arguments/written submissions, if any, with a copy to the other side. Subject to the above, the matter was reserved for order.

- (k) The Respondent did not challenge the notices for recovery sent by the Petitioner. The plea of ‘Force Majeure’ has been invoked as an afterthought in order to set up an excuse for their defaults under the Agreement. In order to justify the defence of the alleged ‘Force Majeure’ condition, it was essential to have set out the action taken by the Respondent against the generating utilities, the correspondence exchanged between the Respondent and the generating utilities, and the conditions of the Agreement executed between the Respondent and the generating utilities. However, no such supporting documents have been placed on record by the Respondent, thereby exposing the hollowness of the Respondent's contentions in the instant reply.

47. Accordingly, Petition No. 278/MP/2022 is disposed of in terms of the above discussions and findings.
